newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline cost cut 10 pct - Metragaz.
newsitem.headline: Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline cost cut 10 pct - Metragaz.

text.p: The Maghreb gas pipeline linking Algeria to markets in Spain and Portugal has been completed at a cost of $1.88 billion, 10.5 percent below estimates, a project director said on Wednesday.
Ignacio Martinez, director of Metragaz, the firm set up to manage the line in Morocco, said gas would start to flow commercially in November.

He told Reuters: "We have been able to cut...the cost of this project compared to base estimates. The total cost for the Algerian, Moroccan and Spanish parties is $1.88 billion, instead of $2.1 billion originally forecast."

Savings had been made particularly in buying the pipes cheaply because of the crisis affecting the European steel industry. This has benefited Morocco, he said, where costs had totalled $880 million instead of $1.1 billion.
Spain's Enagas and the Portuguese Transgas company set up Metragaz to manage the line in Morocco.

The pipeline runs from Hassi R'mel, deep in the Algerian Sahara, across Algeria, northern Morocco, under the Strait of Gibraltar, to Cordoba in Spain. Here it will tie into the Portuguese distribution network and may ultimately expand to supply France and Germany.

The pipeline has a capacity of 9.5 billion cubic metres a year though this may be almost doubled to 18.5 billion under Algeria's plans to double its present gas exports to 60 billion cu metres from the present 30 billion early next century.
Work on the ground for the 1,375 km (860 mile) pipeline started on June 30, 1994.
Morocco's energy ministry secretary-general, Mohammed Seddiki, said the taps would open on October 26, ahead of the commercial operations.
